title: Sell Mineral Rights in Morgantown, WV
metaTitle: Sell Mineral Rights in Morgantown, WV
metaDescription: Morgantown, Monongalia County mineral owners: pioneering Marcellus leasing history, urban-lot severances, and courthouse title verification.
heroLead: Morgantown was ground zero for some of West Virginia's earliest proven Marcellus horizontal wells, and its mineral title today reflects both that pioneering leasing history and the city's growth around WVU.
intro: Wells permitted near the Morgantown Industrial Park in the early 2010s were among the operations that demonstrated horizontal Marcellus drilling could work close to a populated area, and that early success drew steady leasing interest to acreage throughout the city and its surrounding county over the following decade.

At the same time, Morgantown's growth around West Virginia University has meant a lot of mineral acreage within city limits was severed from the surface long before the current homes, apartments, and commercial buildings existed — leaving today's mineral owner and surface owner as frequently unrelated parties.

sections.heading: Early proving ground for the county's Marcellus development
paragraphs: Because Morgantown-area wells were among the first horizontal Marcellus tests in a populated part of the state, some of the leases signed in that first wave carry royalty and bonus terms below what later, more competitive leasing rounds paid elsewhere in Monongalia County. If your family's interest traces to that early period, it's worth comparing your lease terms against what's become standard since, particularly if you're weighing whether to sell or continue holding.

Operators also learned from those early pads, and later units around the city have generally been larger and more efficiently designed — which matters if your acreage was picked up into a more recent unit rather than one of the original test units.

sections.heading: Severed minerals under a growing university city
paragraphs: A meaningful share of Morgantown's mineral acreage was severed from the surface generations ago, before the city's current footprint of subdivisions, student housing, and commercial development existed. The mineral owner today is frequently not the same party as whoever owns the building sitting on top of the tract, and the two interests are tracked entirely separately at the courthouse using the original severance deed's legal description.

This creates real practical friction: modern parcel maps and tax records don't always align cleanly with a 19th- or early 20th-century deed description, so confirming exactly which mineral tract underlies a given piece of current Morgantown real estate takes an actual title search.

sections.heading: Tracing ownership through the Monongalia County Courthouse
paragraphs: Whether your interest traces to an early Marcellus-era lease or an older, unrelated severance, the Monongalia County Courthouse in Morgantown holds the deed, will, and lease records needed to confirm current ownership. Given how much leasing and reassignment activity has occurred in the county over the past decade and a half, it's common for the governing lease on file to be several steps removed from whatever agreement a family remembers signing.

We buy individual heir shares and confirmed fractional interests directly, which is often the fastest path when an estate was never formally probated or when a family group can't reach consensus on whether to sell.

faqs.question: Were Morgantown's early Marcellus leases signed on less favorable terms?
faqs.answer: Some were, since they were signed before the county's leasing market matured. Comparing your lease's royalty and bonus terms against current division orders on similar nearby tracts is worth doing before deciding whether to sell or hold.

faqs.question: Do I own minerals under my Morgantown home or apartment building?
faqs.answer: Not necessarily — check your deed for a mineral reservation. Much of the city's mineral acreage was severed from the surface before current development existed, making the mineral owner and surface owner separate parties in many cases.

faqs.question: How do I match my old deed description to a current Morgantown parcel?
faqs.answer: A title search at the Monongalia County Courthouse, cross-referencing the original severance deed against current tax mapping, will confirm which modern parcel corresponds to your mineral interest.

faqs.question: My family's Morgantown-area interest was never probated — can I sell my share?
faqs.answer: Yes, individual heirs can typically sell their own documented fractional share with a heirship affidavit, without needing a completed probate or full family agreement.
